Terms. An **op spec**, a **class**, the **session sets** and a **capability** are `op-declarations`' (its Terms, R2, R3). The **namespaces** are `bio` and `scratch`. A **bearer** is any caller not arriving by a session. Each refusal below is answered by `control-plane`'s door at the status named, relayed as this module gives it; "is refused" means this module's gate answers that refusal, with the code's `check` and `translation` from its row (R14), and nothing is read or written when it does.
**Namespaces, before any credential is judged** (`namespaceGate`, `confinedNamespaceGate`, `pinnedNamespaceGate`)
- **R1** (was `control-plane` R3) A `store=` that is present and not exactly `bio` or `scratch` is refused 400 `NAMESPACE_UNKNOWN` (C-78.1), naming the namespaces. This applies to every caller and to the instance's page at `/`.
- **R2** (was `control-plane` R4) For an `ai` credential minted confined to `scratch`, a named `store=` other than `scratch` is refused 403 `NAMESPACE_CONFINED` (C-78.3), and an absent one is set to `scratch`.
- **R3** (was `control-plane` R5) A public op that answers only from `bio` refuses `store=scratch` with 400 `NAMESPACE_PINNED` (C-78.2). The public ops that do address scratch are declared (`invitelook`, `enroll`, `instancegroup`, `groupidentity`, and from T34 `websiteinvite`, `joinlinkinvite` and `groupdescription`, since each namespace holds its own key, link and description), and every other public op is pinned. (T40; N797; K2394) `handlecheck` is among them: it reads an invitation, as `invitelook` does.
- **R4** (was `control-plane` R6) Admitted callers land as follows: `probe` in `scratch` (a named other namespace is refused 403 `SCOPE_REFUSED`, C-38.6), and every other class in `scratch` when `store=scratch` is given, else `bio`. Every forwarded answer carries `store`, the namespace that answered.
**Authentication** (`classify`, the agent credential's and the session's resolution)
- **R5** (was `control-plane` R7) A presented credential (R20: the `Authorization` header's, or the body's `token`) equal to the `ADMIN_TOKEN`, `MEMBER_TOKEN`, `PROBE_TOKEN` or `DAEMON_TOKEN` binding (checked in that order) gives that class, but only while the binding is live: set, and not a value ever published (runtime-limits `liveToken`). Any other credential gives no binding class. (T35; F12) Each comparison is of the SHA-256 digests of the two values, in constant time, and all four bindings are compared for every presented credential, so the time taken tells neither whether a binding matched, nor which, nor where two values first differ. (T36) No binding class `member` exists: a presented credential equal to a live `MEMBER_TOKEN` binding gives no class and is refused 401 `MEMBER_TOKEN_RETIRED` (a new row of this module's C-38 family, C-38.11), whose sentence says that the shared member key is retired and that a member signs in with their own password; nothing is read or written. The digests are still compared with all four bindings for every presented credential (R5's constant time), so the time taken does not tell whether a `MEMBER_TOKEN` is bound. With no `MEMBER_TOKEN` bound (the installer writes none, `installer` R9), a value once held is answered as any unknown credential (R7). The refusal is counted as R22 counts kind `credential`.
- **R6** (was `control-plane` R8) A presented credential (R20) shaped `aik-<64 hex>` is resolved once per request against `bio`'s credential rows. A known credential gives class `ai` with its principal, scope and confinement (refused by R10 when revoked or expired). A 64-hex credential is resolved as a session through `credentials.session` (its R5) against `bio`; the `aik-` lookup is `credentials.aiCredentialLook` (its R15). Each lookup carries the credential to the store in a request body or as its SHA-256, never in the address of the store's request (R20). A store that does not answer either lookup is answered 502 `STORE_DID_NOT_ANSWER` and never as a statement about the caller.
- **R7** (was `control-plane` R9) A caller with no class is refused 401 `NOT_AUTHENTICATED` (C-38.1).
**Admission, in this order**
- **R8** (was `control-`store-assembly` R100) A session reaching a mutating op outside its kind's session set is refused 403. The refusal depends on why. `SESSION_ROLE_CANNOT_REACH_OP` (C-38.7) is used when the other kind's set holds the op, with `reachedBy` set to `founder` or `member`. `MACHINE_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED` (C-38.3) is used when a recorded decision reserves the op to a credential, and cites that decision. `SESSION_ROUTE_NOT_RECORDED` (C-38.8) is used when no decision is recorded. `capture`'s GET is a read. `export` is admitted to the root-of-trust bearer (R9) and to the founder's session (kind `admin`), the session the claim made from that token (Membership v2 §4.6); a session of any other kind, an enrolled administrator's included, is refused `ROOT_OF_TRUST_REQUIRED` (C-38.4), before R9 and R11 (K4245).
- **R9** (was `control-plane` R11) A binding class not in the op's `classes` is refused 403 `CLASS_FORBIDDEN` (C-38.2). For a caller that did not arrive by a session, `machineClasses` is used instead where the spec gives it.
- **R10** (was `control-plane` R12) An `ai` caller is refused `AI_CREDENTIAL_REVOKED` (C-29.7) when its credential is withdrawn. It is refused `AI_BEYOND_TASK_SCOPE` (C-29.6) when no member reaches the op, or when the op is mutating and not among its declared writes. (T35; K1934 (5); `credentials` R42) It is refused `AI_CREDENTIAL_EXPIRED` (401, a new C-29 row) when `credentials.aiCredentialLook` answers its credential `expired: true`, as a revoked one is refused, before any scope is judged; a credential both revoked and expired is answered `AI_CREDENTIAL_REVOKED`. Either refusal is counted as R22 states.
- **R11** (was `control-plane` R13) A session missing the op's capability is refused 403 `NOT_CAPABLE` (C-38.5), naming `needs` and `held`. A binding class holds no capabilities and is bounded by R9 alone. A session creating a project (a promotion with no base whose promoted type is `project`) without `create_projects` is refused the same 403 `NOT_CAPABLE` (C-38.5), `needs: "create_projects"`, `held` sorted, whatever NEEDS says of `promote` (K723; one site, `projectCreationGate`).
- **R12** (was `control-plane` R14) A bearer (any caller not arriving by a session) asking for a §4 governance act (`adminendorse`, `adminremove`, `membercaps`) is refused 403 `OPERATOR_TOKEN_CANNOT_GOVERN` (C-32.17). Asking for a group-identity act (`groupnameset`, `groupdomainset`), it is refused `GROUP_IDENTITY_NEEDS_SESSION` (C-64.4). Each refusal names the class.
**An agent credential's scope, at the mint** (`aiScopeDeclaration`, `aiConfinementDeclaration`)
- **R13** (was `control-plane` R19) An agent credential's scope is judged when it is minted. An op no spec declares is refused `AI_SCOPE_UNKNOWN_OP` (C-29.8). An op no member reaches is refused `AI_SCOPE_BEYOND_MEMBER_REACH` (C-29.9). A `confinedTo` other than absent or exactly `scratch` is refused `AI_CONFINEMENT_NOT_SCRATCH` (C-29.10). The credential's value and a review grant's secret are generated here, returned once in the minting answer, and passed on only as their SHA-256. An op a bearer is refused by R12 counts as beyond member reach, both at the mint and in R10.
**The doors into the group** (DEC-133; `membership` R101, R104, R105; `op-declarations` R22)
- **R17** `websiteinvite` (the group's website's call) and `joinlinkinvite` (the join page's call) are public ops: each is admitted with no credential, and a credential or session presented with either is neither required nor used. Whoever calls, nothing about the caller reaches the act: it is recorded only as its door's (`website:<keyId>`, `join-link:<linkId>`, `membership` R105), never as a signed-in member, a binding class or an `ai` credential. The key or link and the cover are read from the request's body only; one sent in the query is not read (so a secret is never kept in an address), and the call then answers as `membership` answers a missing key or link. Admission adds no limit of its own: the daily cap is `membership`'s (`WEBSITE_DAILY_CAP`, `JOIN_LINK_DAILY_CAP`), relayed by the door (`answer-envelope` R4), and R15 holds: no key, link or invitation appears in any refusal this module answers. (T35; F4) The one limit admission adds is R21's per-source window, which holds over these doors as over every credential-free request; the daily caps are unchanged.
- **R18** (K1749) The administrator's acts `op-declarations` R22 declares are admitted as their specs say and reach `membership`, whose own refusal answers a caller who is not an administrator (`NOT_AN_ADMIN`, its R84), a machine credential included; R12's bearer fences do not name them and this module adds no fence for them.
**The group's API key** (K1755; `credentials` R33, R34, R36; `op-declarations` R24)
- **R19** The ops `op-declarations` R24 declares (`groupkeyset`, `groupkeyremove`, `groupkeyswitch`, `groupkeystate`, `groupkeynotice`, `groupkeynoticeseen`; `groupswitchset` retired to `accountusesset`, DEC-188 (8)) are admitted only from a session: a bearer, a machine credential and an operator token are refused by R9 (`CLASS_FORBIDDEN`, their specs' `machineClasses` being empty), naming the class, an `ai` credential by R10 (`AI_BEYOND_TASK_SCOPE`, C-29.6; K1863), and an ask's grant as `credentials` R28 refuses an op not on `AI_GRANT_OPS` (`GRANT_OP_REFUSED`), each before any store call. A member's session reaches `credentials`, whose own refusal answers a caller who is not an administrator (`NOT_AN_ADMIN`, its R33); since R29 this module asks that question first, before any password check, and answers the same `NOT_AN_ADMIN`. `groupkeyset`'s key is read from the request's body only: a key sent in the query is not read (so the key is never kept in an address), and the call then answers as `credentials` answers an empty key (`NO_SECRET`). R15 holds: the key appears in no refusal this module answers.
**Where a credential is read, who is calling, and the door's window** (T35; F1, F4, K1874, K1881; N703)
- **R20** (F1; K1874; K2111) A credential travels in a request's header or body, never in an address. `presentedCredential({req, url, body})` answers `{token, secret, inAddress}` and never throws: (K2576; `op-declarations` R42) `handlecheck`'s `invite` and `handle` are body-only too (`BODY_ONLY_FIELDS`): a query's copy is stripped, and a request naming its invitation only in the query is answered `NO_SUCH_INVITATION`, as R17's doors answer a missing key.
- `token` (a session token, an `aik-` credential, an ask's grant or a binding token) is read from the `Authorization` header when it is exactly `Bearer <value>` (the scheme in any case, one space, a value of printable characters with no space); else, for a request with a JSON object body, from its `token` field when that is a non-empty string; never from the address. An `Authorization` header in any other form presents no `token`.
- `secret` (a review grant's or a template grant's secret, `control-plane` R20, R44) is read from the JSON body's `secret` field; never from the address.
- `inAddress` is `true` exactly when the request's address names a `token` or a `secret` parameter, whatever its value and whether or not the header or body carries one too.
A request whose `inAddress` is `true` is refused 400 `CREDENTIAL_IN_ADDRESS` (C-38.10) by this module's gate `credentialAddressGate(url)` (answering `null`, or `{status: 400, body}` as this module's other gates do; K2157), which `control-plane` runs directly after R1 (its R28), before any credential is judged, any public op runs or the store is asked: the value is never compared, looked up, passed on or logged, and the refusal names neither it nor its digest (R15). It is the code's one site (K231): `publication`'s door does not answer it (its R73), and no answer carries `deprecated`. Every gate of this module (R5–R13, R16, R19, R21) judges the credential `presentedCredential` answers and no other, and this module places no credential, secret or digest of either in the address of any request it makes, the store's internal requests included. A test sends a sentinel credential by header and by body to one op of each kind (a session's, an `ai` credential's, a binding class's, a grant's door, a review door, a public op) and finds the same admission as before; by the address, alone and beside a header, it finds C-38.10, no request to the store, and the sentinel in no answer and no address of any request the plane makes.
- **R21** (F4; K1881; `doorbell` R12, was `capture` R56 until T43 (K2708); DEC-166) Who is calling is known only as a keyed fingerprint and a country. `sourceOf(req, env)` answers the keyed fingerprint of the connecting address (the address as Cloudflare states it, `CF-Connecting-IP`), made as `doorbell` R12 makes one (HMAC-SHA-256 under the same key), or one shared source of its own when the request states no address. (T38; N792; K2247) When the `KNOCK_FINGERPRINT_KEY` binding is unbound, the key is only in the store (`doorbell` R12's instance key), and `sourceOf` answers the fingerprint the store makes of the address under it, asked through the store-internal `doorwindow` route with `count: false`, which counts, refuses and writes nothing. So for one address `setpassword`'s `source` (`control-plane` R68) equals `login`'s (the window's, `control-plane` R58) with or without the binding, and `credentials` R38's sign-in window counts them as one source. When the store cannot be asked, `sourceOf` answers `null` as before, logged by correlation id only, and never throws; `countryOf(req)` answers Cloudflare's two-letter country label for the request (`request.cf.country`), or `null`. Neither keeps, logs or answers the address. `control-plane` stamps both on the ops that take them (`credentials` R1, R4, R47's `source` and `country`; `capture` R85's `country`). Every request to a public op (`classes: null`, `op-declarations` R2: among them the doors of R17, `claim`, `login`, `recover`, `enroll`, `invitelook`, the review and template doors reached by a secret, and the public reads), whoever calls and whatever it presents, is counted against one window per source: at most 300 such requests per source in any 10 minutes, estimated by a two-bucket sliding window (`prev × (1 − elapsed/W) + cur`, W 10 minutes; `capture` R31's form), refused at `≥ 300` with 429 `DOOR_RATE_LIMITED` (a new row of this module's C-38 family) carrying `stated`, the bound composed from the same constants, and `retryAfter` in whole seconds, as the first gate of the public ops (`control-plane` R28's order), before the op runs, so nothing of the op is read or written. A request to an op that is not public is never counted or refused by this window (a caller with no credential is refused it by R7). A refused request is not counted again. The counts hold the fingerprint, the bucket and the count, nothing else, and are dropped once both buckets have passed. A count that cannot be read or written admits the request (the window fails open, so a fault in it never refuses a caller) and is named in the log by correlation id only. `recover`, `claim` and `login` stay also under `credentials` R38's sign-in window, which is `credentials`' own. (Fix round 10, cause 27b; K5057) The window's counts are kept in memory and written to the store at most every 5 seconds; the limit is judged from the counts in memory, and an object restarting loses at most the last 5 seconds of counts. Test: fifty counted requests change at most two rows; controls: the 301st request in ten minutes is still refused, and two sources are counted apart.
- **R22** (N703; K1875; the store write through `securitycount` deferred by K2038 to T36, N744, as credentials' map has no such route; DEC-165, DEC-166; `credentials` R44) Refused keys and links and over-the-limit requests are counted in `credentials`' security tally, through `credentials.securityCount({kind, country})` (its R44), once per refusal, by `securityTally({op, answer, presented, req})`, which this module answers for each refusal it gives and `control-plane` calls for each refusal it relays: kind `credential` for an `ai` caller refused `AI_CREDENTIAL_REVOKED` or `AI_CREDENTIAL_EXPIRED` (R10), an `aik-`-shaped credential no row knows, `op=invitelook` or `op=enroll` answered `NO_SUCH_INVITATION` (`membership` R15, R16, R97: an expired or unknown invitation), `op=websiteinvite` answered `WEBSITE_KEY_UNKNOWN` (`membership` R101) and `op=joinlinkinvite` answered `NO_SUCH_JOIN_LINK` (its R104); kind `rate` for R21's `DOOR_RATE_LIMITED` and for `WEBSITE_DAILY_CAP` and `JOIN_LINK_DAILY_CAP` relayed. `country` is `countryOf(req)` (R21), except `null` for a refused request that presents a credential naming a member (a session, or an agent credential whose principal is a member), so no member is placed (DEC-166 (2)). Nothing else of the request reaches the count: no address, fingerprint, credential, handle, role, op or time within the hour. Every other refusal and every admitted request is not counted. A count that cannot be written is dropped and never changes the refusal's answer, its status or its order. The count reaches `credentials` in-plane, through the store's internal route `securitycount`, which no caller reaches (`op-declarations` R6). (T36; N744, K2038) Its count reaches `credentials` through the store's internal route `securitycount` (`credentials` R50, merged in T36-7), and it also counts R5's `MEMBER_TOKEN_RETIRED` as kind `credential`. (T40; N797; K2394) It counts `op=handlecheck` answered `NO_SUCH_INVITATION` (`membership` R123) as kind `credential`, as it counts `invitelook`'s.
#### T49: words by key (K3366, K3368; DEC-257, DEC-258)
- **R28** (T49; K3366; DEC-257, DEC-258; `setup-words` R11–R13; amends every requirement here that quotes a member-facing sentence) **Words by key.** This module holds no member-facing English: every sentence it draws or answers is read through `setup-words` `word(key, vars)`, and the module holds only keys. Its keys are the `reads` list for it in `docs/development/ux-substrate/screens/words-reads.json` (DEC-258; its keys as R31 lists them), with any key a requirement here names. A sentence an earlier requirement here quotes means the key whose English it is: the quotation identifies the key and binds no wording, so a word changed in `words.json` changes no requirement and no code here. The 35 strings that list marks `unkeyed` (none read by a member, each with its reason) stay in source. Test: each key it reads is asserted with `setup-words` `hasWord`; over fixtures, what it draws for a sample of its keys equals `word(key, vars)`; no test holds a sentence's English.
#### T51 fix round 8 (K4817; `build/plan/archive/fix-round-8-T51.md`)
- **R32** (fix round 8, G119; K4814 (4), K4817) **One session read per request.** One request through `gate`, `readerOf` and `liveSessionDigest` reads its session once (a memo for that request only); `doorwindow` stays (a protective limit, K1881). Test: one session read per request (red: three); through the door `groupidentity` makes three object calls.
- **R34** (T53; N1264, K4599 (a); `platform/combined-read-and-fold-draft.md` PL12; amends R1–R12, R14, R33) **`admit` is callable from inside the room.** The judgement stays this module's, pure, and `store-door` calls it from inside the room with the session row the room holds (`resolveSession` is the one part that runs beside the session rows). Every refusal of R1–R12 and R14 (codes, statuses, `check`, `translation`) is answered exactly as now, in the same order, whether admission runs at the door or in the room. Test: a parity table: every refusal code of R1–R12 and R14 judged both ways with the same answer; the order test (R8 before R9 before R10 before R11).
- **R35** (T53; N1264, K4599 (a); `platform/combined-read-and-fold-draft.md` PL13; amends R27) **The folded path counts as the unfolded one does.** The folded path counts `background` and the door window exactly as the unfolded one (door order and `background` counting kept); a bearer (a caller by no session) is judged at the door and makes no extra call. Test: the window's count after N folded calls equals its count after N unfolded calls. Control: a bearer's call makes no call to the room beyond the op's own.
